note: Hebrew chavatselet is a bulb flower of the plain (crocus, asphodel or narcissus), not a rose; the KJV's article also makes it a title.

mine: Sustain me (the woman) with raisin cakes
note: Hebrew 'ashishot are pressed raisin cakes (2 Sam 6:19, Hos 3:1), not flasks of wine.

kjv: nor awake [my] love, till he please
mine: or awaken love until it pleases
note: Hebrew ha'ahavah is "love" itself (abstract, with the article), and techpats "it pleases" (fem.). The KJV supplies "my" and "he", making it the sleeping beloved rather than a warning not to rouse passion prematurely.
Hebrew tor is the turtledove; "turtle" for the bird is obsolete and now suggests the reptile.
